One of the most important thing about reporting is source citation. This process has to start as soon as the research begins. It's incredibly more difficult to search for your source than to note it down when discovering the article/photo/... I am currently looking at Zotero to see if it's a viable option for collaborated source citing and collection.

There are three popular styles: MLA, APA, and CMS. Their differences can be found in this pdf file. Right now I'm leaning towards CMS, a much used and very well documented style.

If I wanted to have a huge amount of video-games (something like this), where would I start? I considered simply looking up the games that I wanted on Amazon & eBay, but before going on a shopping spree I wanted to know if there was some place where I could get them really cheap.

The games I'm looking for are under the following platforms:

  • Nintendo Wii / WiiU
  • PlayStation 2 / PS3 / PS4
  • Xbox 360

Though I'll still take games for older generations (like N64 and Genesis) if you can find them.
Creating A Large Gaming Library. Any reputable places where I can find cheap games?
Lot's of classic games are now on archive.org to be used for emulators, not physical cartridges though.

I'd skip retail venues and hit up garage sales. It may be the most time-consuming, but overall most rewarding... you never know what treasures you may find. My best advice is go to the middle-class neighborhoods in late summer, when the college kids are moving out and the parents are desperately getting rid of anything in sight; baby boomers like to ditch their collections during this time, too.

Learn to haggle and bundle as much as possible. While the internet and price checking are available to anyone, video games (especially vintage) are generally glossed over and sold for dirt cheap.

Last summer I bought a Sega CDX w/ box for $5! Also snagged a few mint SNES titles, most notably Earthbound and Super Metroid.

Back in college there was local collectables store that sold everything from model trains to trading cards and they had one of the best selection of old games I'd ever seen for purchase ranging from Atari through the new releases. It's where I grabbed my Mario Kart and Mortal Kombat which are fun to break out now and again on drunken weekends.

I'd agree with /u/HotPockets and say keep an eye out for yard sales / garage sales but to also look into nearby pawn shops or collectible stores as well.

As for newer games, eBay (as you mentioned) occasionally will have sellers looking to offload bunches of games for cheap (not always great but cheap). Amazon might have a "better selection" but it won't have the bulk that eBay might have.
Never underestimate what you can find at a pawn shop. They kept me playing a new PS2 game every week.
